transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (BlueWave Eng Lead), Maya Rao (BlueWave PM), Ellen Kim (BlueWave Security), Omar Aziz (BlueWave Infra)
Artifacts referenced: Benchmark spreadsheet (shortlink: /sheets/bw-bench-03), Security pack (link: /docs/bw-secpack), Staging VPC runbook (link note)

Summary:
Quick triage of last week's benchmarking run — multi-model tail latency spikes and gateway auth failures in the staging environment. Agreed next steps: share traces, validate RBAC/STS roles, and run a dedicated high-throughput job with quantization profile recommended by Redwood.

Topics covered:
- infra credentials & staging VPC readiness
- latency profile / tail latencies and KV cache hit rates
- gateway eligibility / 401s observed during burst test
- security & compliance materials (SOC2, KMS integration)
- plan for next dedicated benchmark and acceptance criteria

Action items (read out):
- Diego to export trimmed traces + sticky-keys split
- Omar to share IAM policy and staging creds (limited)
- Laura to send SOC2 docs and bench sheet

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, and then Diego will walk through the perf traces we pulled from staging earlier this week.
[00:18] Samir (BlueWave): Hey, thanks Laura. We had a weird flake where the gateway returned 401s intermittently during the spike test, so we're hoping to pin that down.
[00:28] Laura: Right, that's one of the things Diego flagged, along with tail latency spikes around 95th and 99th percentiles. Diego?
[00:35] Diego (Redwood): Yep hi. I pulled the traces, and there are two patterns. One is auth retries that line up with credential refresh failures — looks like short-lived STS tokens from the role used in staging. The other is a KV cache miss surge when we switched to the longer context tests, which caused backlog and batching to change.
[01:02] Diego: Sorry, um, to clarify — the KV cache mis, miss rate rose from ~4% to 22% when sequence length hit >2k, and that pushed additional work onto the serving nodes so you see tail spikes.
[01:16] Omar (BlueWave): Quick q — are those serving-side cache misses or client-side? We did change our prefixing logic in the client between runs.
[01:25] Diego: Mostly serving-side — we saw KV cache eviction and less beneficial prefix reuse. There's also an interplay with batching: when the client sends a long request, continuous batching groups fewer requests and that hurt per-token throughput.
[01:45] Maya (BlueWave): Got it. We did change prefixing, that's true. We can flip it back for a run. Also, about the 401s — Ellen, is that on your radar?
[01:53] Ellen (BlueWave Security): Yeah, we saw the audit logs. Looks like the AWS STS tokens that the gateway service assumes are expiring earlier than we expected. Might be an assume-role TTL mismatch. We'll confirm the token refresh window.
[02:08] Priya (Redwood CSM): Thanks, Ellen. If you can send the token policy we can map it to Redwood's SDK's refresh behavior. We have a small doc that describes expected TTLs for seamless rotation.
[02:20] Laura: On the security side we did send SOC2 summary last week, but i'll re-send the packet with network diagrams. Also Diego, can you summarize the quantization profile suggestion?
[02:32] Diego: Sure. For this workload we recommend 4-bit q4_k_m quant for initial runs; gives about ~1.6x throughput improvement with minimal quality drop for prompt completions up to 2k tokens. For >2k token sequences, q4 may increase jitter — but it's still net positive. We'll attach recommended config in the bench sheet.
[02:56] Samir: Wait — jitter as in tail latency variability, right? Not hallucination risk?
[03:03] Diego: Correct, jitter = latency variance. QA/quality impact is small for your prompts, but we should include a small eval set to validate generation quality post-quant.
[03:12] Maya: We have an eval set of ~200 prompts we used in staging; happy to share.
[03:18] Diego: Perfect. If you share that we'll add the automatic quality regression checks into the run.
[03:25] Omar: Back to the gateway 401s — I'm going to drop a limited set of staging creds into the shared vault, marked for read-only and assume-role. Should have that by tomorrow.
[03:34] Ellen: Also, to note, our security team wants KMS integration and a diagram of where keys are used — we don't want any service to log raw prompts.
[03:42] Laura: Understood, Ellen — Redwood's private deployments support customer-managed KMS keys; for the hosted pilot we can show the key flow and scrub logs. I'll attach the network diagram and the KMS note.
[03:55] Samir: Another oddity — during the 10k concurrent token run, one of the pods reported OOM Warnings before the spike. Wondering if that's the quant profile mismatch?
[04:05] Diego: Could be. OOMs can happen if batch sizing changes due to sequence-length distribution. We're going to instrument more detailed memory traces on the next run. I'll also show per-batch memory footprints in the bench sheet.
[04:18] Maya: Good. Can we also get a per-request token cost estimate? Product wants to understand unit economics at 95th percentile.
[04:26] Laura: We can supply token cost models — Diego, we have the per-request cost breakout in the optimize tool, right?
[04:32] Diego: Yeah we'll export that. It shows per-token CPU/GPU cost and batched amortization. For your config, I expect ~15-18% cost improvement with q4 and KV prefix caching.
[04:45] Samir: Sounds reasonable. About acceptance criteria — what would we need to see to mark the benchmark as successful?
[04:50] Priya: From Redwood's perspective, typical POC acceptance is: sustained throughput at your target QPS with 95th latency under X ms (we'll set X after seeing your SLO), stable error rate < 0.1%, and no auth failures during a continuous 30-minute run.
[05:05] Maya: Our initial SLO target is 95th < 280ms and errors <0.05% for production traffic patterns.
[05:13] Laura: Ok we'll aim to replicate that in staging. One ask — can you provide a short sampled production traffic pattern or a synthetic replay? That helps us match batching and prefix distributions.
[05:23] Omar: We will run a sanitized trace and share tomorrow. It's small — just metadata and token counts, no PII.
[05:31] Diego: Great — once we have that, we'll run a dedicated benchmark with q4 profile and the eval set. We'll also enable sticky KV caching and track cache hit rates.
[05:43] Maya: Timeline?
[05:45] Laura: Ideal: creds and traces by 2027-03-11, Redwood delivers revised bench config + traces by 2027-03-12, run scheduled 2027-03-14 (morning UTC).
[05:57] Samir: That works. Ellen, any blockers on your side for creds?
[06:01] Ellen: Just need to confirm least-privilege policy; otherwise fine.
[06:05] Diego: Small note — we saw ephemeral gateway 502s correlated with a single model variant hitting a slow path. We'll attach the stack traces; could be kernel selection on that node.
[06:16] Laura: We'll put an action item to isolate the model variant and run it on a different hardware profile if necessary.
[06:23] Omar: Can Redwood also provide a short runbook for fallback policy — e.g., how to fail over to a lower-capacity model in case of sustained tail issues?
[06:31] Priya: Yes — Redwood supports policy-based routing; we'll provide a draft canary/fallback plan and an example config.
[06:38] Maya: Great. A couple of small asks: please include the raw latency traces and a simple chart we can paste into the exec update.
[06:46] Laura: We'll include charts in the bench sheet export. Diego, anything else to call out?
[06:51] Diego: Just that the next run will include per-batch memory dumps, cache hit timeline, and auth refresh logs. That should let us correlate the 401s and OOMs precisely.
[07:03] Samir: Awesome. Last q — you mentioned SOC2 docs, can i get a short answer on data retention policy for the pilot?
[07:11] Laura: For the hosted pilot we retain logs for 30 days by default but we can scope retention, and we redact prompts unless you opt-in to share. For Private deployment you control retention via your KMS and log store. I'll confirm exact retention numbers in the packet.
[07:27] Ellen: Please also include the audit log format and an example.
[07:31] Laura: Will do.
[07:33] Priya: Recap and next steps — Diego to export trimmed perf traces by 2027-03-12, Omar to provide limited staging creds by 2027-03-11, Laura to send SOC2 and bench sheet link today, schedule dedicated run for 2027-03-14.
[07:48] Maya: Thanks all. If we hit the SLO in the dedicated run we want to start discussing Dedicated capacity pricing — maybe a 3-month reserved window.
[07:58] Laura: Noted, we'll prep a ballpark for the next sync.
[08:02] Samir: Good meeting, thanks.
[08:06] Meeting end
